svg.title: Figure 3-2a. The trust boundaries, one by one (WP-S-07 §3.2), animated
svg.desc: Trust boundaries of WP-S-07 §3.2, one per frame: TB-3 Z4 ↔ Z3 network, 22 controls, 3 in place, 2 partly, 15 not met, 2 not determined; TB-6 Z6 → device, 7 controls, 0 in place, 1 partly, 6 not met, 0 not determined; TB-4 Z3 → Z2 local integrity, 9 controls, 2 in place, 1 partly, 5 not met, 1 not determined; TB-1 Z2 → Z1 command channel (SPI/USB), 11 controls, 3 in place, 6 partly, 2 not met, 0 not determined; TB-2 Z2 → Z1 boot control (GPIO), 7 controls, 0 in place, 1 partly, 6 not met, 0 not determined; TB-5 Z1 ↔ Z5 vehicle CAN, 3 controls, 0 in place, 3 partly, 0 not met, 0 not determined; TB-7 Z7 physical, 6 controls, 0 in place, 2 partly, 0 not met, 4 not determined.

g.text: Terms: AGNOS the comma device's operating system · CAN controller area network: the
vehicle's data bus · CSR-nn cybersecurity requirement: CSR-C-nn at concept level
(WP-C-10 §7), CSR-nnn refined (WP-S-07) · GPIO general-purpose input/output pin · LFS
Git Large File Storage (where the model files live) · MCU microcontroller: the panda
safety processor (STM32H7) · PCS pre-collision system: Toyota's stock collision warning
and braking · RPC remote procedure call · RX receive · SoC system on chip: the comma
device's main processor, running openpilot (QM) · SPI serial peripheral interface (the
link between SoC and MCU) · SSH secure shell (remote login) · TB-nn trust boundary
(WP-S-07 §3.2) · TS-nn threat scenario (TARA §4) · TX transmit · USB universal serial
bus (on the panda, a second host link the reference device does not use) · WP-nn work
product, e.g. WP-C-04; the letter is its area (M management, C concept, S system, H
hardware, W software, V validation, P processes, A analyses, O operation, K safety case)
